speaker: Doctor
text: That is very helpful. Since your pain is shooting and started after your tympanoplasty, could you describe the specific location of the pain and whether it radiates to your forehead or teeth?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient has a history of polycystic ovarian syndrome, depression, and chronic bilateral ear infections. She underwent right ear tympanoplasty 12 weeks ago. Although audiology report from one week ago showed improved hearing by 20 decibels, she reports occasional shooting pain when eating and discomfort when wearing earrings. She describes her job as stressful and mentions poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the detailed history. Is the shooting ear pain triggered specifically by chewing or swallowing, and does the discomfort from earrings persist even if you avoid wearing them? Also, have you noticed any fluid discharge or changes in hearing since the surgery?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Occasional shooting pain in the ear with eating. I also have Discomfort when wearing earrings, Stress from job, Poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Trigeminal Neuralgia (specifically V2 distribution) secondary to post-surgical irritation or entrapment of the mandibular nerve during tympanoplasty. The shooting pain triggered by chewing is classic for this condition, and the "earring discomfort" is likely referred pain from the same nerve pathway rather than direct mechanical pressure.

REQUEST TEST: MRI of the head with contrast focusing on the trigeminal nerve and mastoid air cells.
REQUEST IMAGES: High-resolution CT of the temporal bone.
